name: Birds of Stone Intentional Camera Movement Rubric v1
description: Experimental rubric for photographs using intentional camera movement, slow-shutter trails, flash-drag, zoom, or related motion techniques. Blur and distortion are evaluated as design material rather than automatic defects.

dimensions.label: Intentional Motion
dimensions.description: How successfully motion, retained detail, light, and subject information combine into an intentional photographic result.

facets.label: Motion Structure
facets.prompt: Do blur, trails, streaks, repetition, stretch, or zoom effects form a coherent visible structure rather than undirected mush?

facets.label: Directional Coherence
facets.prompt: Do the direction, rhythm, acceleration, and spatial distribution of movement support the frame's composition and energy?

facets.label: Layering and Repetition
facets.prompt: Where present, do overlapping positions, repeated forms, flash echoes, or light layers create useful depth, rhythm, or visual relationships?

facets.label: Subject Anchor
facets.prompt: When the image needs one, is there enough retained subject, gesture, face, silhouette, light, or shape to give the movement a meaningful anchor? Use N/A when complete abstraction is visibly the intended result.

facets.label: Motion-Sharpness Contrast
facets.prompt: Where retained sharpness or frozen detail is present, does its contrast with moving areas strengthen the image? Sharpness is not required and should not be rewarded merely for existing.

facets.label: Flash-Freeze Integration
facets.prompt: Where flash or another freezing mechanism is visible, is the frozen layer integrated coherently with ambient motion, trails, or repeated subject positions? Use N/A when no frozen layer is present.

facets.label: Energy and Emotional Impact
facets.prompt: Does the motion treatment communicate performance energy, atmosphere, tension, intimacy, chaos, humour, speed, or another clear emotional effect?

facets.label: Movement Intentionality
facets.prompt: Does the movement appear deliberately directed, timed, or composed for this frame rather than simply caused by an uncontrolled slow exposure?

facets.label: Distinctiveness
facets.prompt: Does the motion treatment produce a memorable visual idea or relationship rather than a generic blur effect?

facets.label: Intent-Appropriate Legibility
facets.prompt: Is the amount of recognisable subject or scene information appropriate to the photograph's visible intent, including cases where deliberate abstraction is the goal?

facets.label: Uncontrolled Smear and Obstruction Control
facets.prompt: Are accidental smears, blocked subjects, dead areas, flash timing failures, or visual collisions controlled enough that the intended motion effect remains effective?
